title: Bharat Vidhi & Civic Core (Law & Citizen Rights)
description: Indian Constitution, legal safeguards, consumer protection, new criminal laws (BNS/BNSS), police FIR procedures, and citizen helplines.

chunks.title: National Emergency Helpline Numbers
chunks.text: National Emergency Unified Helpline: 112 (Police, Fire, Ambulance). Police: 100, Fire: 101, Ambulance: 108. Women Helpline (National): 1091 and 181. National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: 1930. Childline Helpline: 1098. Senior Citizen Helpline (Elderline): 14567. Railway Security Helpline: 139. Disaster Management Helpline: 1078.

chunks.title: Filing a Police FIR (First Information Report) & Zero FIR
chunks.text: Under Section 173 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) / Section 154 CrPC, an officer in charge must register an FIR upon information of a cognizable offence. A citizen has the legal right to receive a signed copy of the FIR immediately and free of cost. If a crime occurred outside police station jurisdiction, police must register a 'Zero FIR' and transfer it later. Refusal to register FIR is punishable under law.

chunks.title: Fundamental Rights Guaranteed by Constitution of India
chunks.text: Part III of the Indian Constitution enshrines 6 Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22, including speech and expression), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32 - enabling citizens to approach Supreme Court directly via habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari).

chunks.title: Right to Information (RTI Act 2005) Process
chunks.text: Any Indian citizen can request information from a Public Authority under RTI Act 2005. Standard application fee is ₹10 (exempt for Below Poverty Line applicants). The Public Information Officer (PIO) must supply the information within 30 days. If the matter involves life or liberty of a person, information must be provided within 48 hours.

chunks.title: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Remedies
chunks.text: Under Consumer Protection Act 2019, consumers can file e-complaints via the e-Daakhil portal without needing a lawyer. District Commissions adjudicate claims up to ₹50 Lakh, State Commissions up to ₹2 Crore, and National Commission above ₹2 Crore. Covers unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, defective goods, and deficiency in services.

chunks.title: Cybercrime Financial Fraud Golden Hour (Helpline 1930)
chunks.text: If victimized by financial cyber fraud (UPI fraud, phishing, credit card scam), immediately dial 1930 within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2-4 hours). The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) coordinates with banks to freeze transferred funds in the fraudster's account before withdrawal. Also lodge complaint on cybercrime.gov.in.

chunks.title: Rights of an Arrested Person
chunks.text: Under Article 22 of Constitution and BNSS/CrPC: 1. Police must inform the grounds of arrest immediately. 2. Right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice. 3. Right to free legal aid via DLSA if indigent. 4. Right to have a friend or relative informed of the arrest. 5. Must be produced before the nearest Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding journey time).

chunks.title: Traffic Police Rules & DigiLocker Digital Documents
chunks.text: Under Rule 139 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, citizens can present Driving License (DL), Registration Certificate (RC), and Insurance electronically via Government DigiLocker or mParivahan apps. Traffic police must accept these as legally equivalent to original physical cards. Police cannot seize physical documents if digital versions are presented.
